pages.text: The run and the rise meet at a right angle, so the long side from A to B is the hypotenuse, and Pythagoras gives its length, `d`. Square the run and the rise, add, then take the square root, `√(36 + 64) = √100 = 10`. Written with the coordinates, that is the [[distance formula]], and it works wherever you drag A or B.

pages.text: Half the run is 3 and half the rise is 4, so the [[midpoint]] is `(1 + 3, 2 + 4) = (4, 6)`. It sits on the long side, because half the run along gives half the rise up. Along, 4 is 3 on from 1 and 3 short of 7, so it is halfway, and halfway between two numbers is their average: `(1 + 7) ÷ 2 = 4`, and likewise `(2 + 10) ÷ 2 = 6`.

pages.why: The average of the x's is `(2 + 8) ÷ 2 = 5` and of the y's `(3 + 7) ÷ 2 = 5`, so the midpoint is (5, 5). That is half the run, 3, along from A and half the rise, 2, up.
